description: A designer's or consultant's portfolio, judged by someone hiring.

journey.audience: A hiring manager or design lead screening candidates for the role.
journey.endsAt: A way to get in touch (contact details or a contact form). Nothing is sent.

stages.name: Arrive and orient
stages.task: You're hiring for this role and arrive from a link in a message. What do you do first?
checks: The first screen says who this is and what they do, in plain words
The kind of work (domain, research, product) is clear without scrolling
One primary action (see the work) stands out

stages.name: Find the work
stages.task: You want to see their most relevant project. Where do you click?
checks: A case study is one click from the first screen
Projects are labelled by the problem or outcome, not only a client name or image
The most relevant project for the role can be picked out without opening them all

stages.name: Judge the evidence
stages.task: You're on a case study. Find what this person did personally, and what changed because of it.
checks: The person's own role is stated
An outcome or evidence is stated, or why it can't be shared
A summary near the top gives the problem, role and outcome

stages.name: Get in touch
stages.task: You'd like to invite them to interview. How do you get in touch?
checks: A contact route is visible from the case study, not just the homepage
Contact needs no form, or the form asks only for essentials
Availability or what happens next is stated

stages.name: Reassurance
stages.task: Before reaching out, you want to check they're credible. Where do you look?
checks: Independent proof (a named testimonial, publication or client) sits near the work
Real identity is clear: full name, LinkedIn, location
The site looks current: dates, current role

exampleTasks: Find their email, starting from a case study
Find a project about <the role's domain>
Find where they studied or trained
Find what they're working on now
